The findings will be presented in a final evaluation report, which will be made publicly available, and will be discussed with stakeholders through a stakeholder workshop.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) operational and advocacy support for refugees, internally displaced persons, and irregular migrants in meeting their short- and long-term food security and nutrition needs. The evaluation employed a mixed-methods approach, combining desk reviews, interviews, and case studies to assess WFP's strategic vision, programme approaches, and partnerships in supporting these vulnerable populations. Key findings indicate that while WFP has made significant contributions to addressing immediate food security needs, its ability to support self-reliance at scale is limited due to a historical focus on grant funding and a lack of clear business propositions. Furthermore, WFP's assistance modalities and programming approaches are not always contextualized to meet the specific needs and vulnerabilities of different categories of persons on the move. The evaluation also highlights the importance of WFP's relationships with governments, regional institutions, and international partners in accessing and supporting refugees, internally displaced persons, and irregular migrants. However, the evaluation notes that WFP's ability to engage in durable solutions and protection of these populations is hindered by a lack of clarity on roles and responsibilities, as well as limited engagement with governments and cooperating partners. Overall, the evaluation suggests that WFP needs to enhance its strategic vision, programme approaches, and partnerships to better support the long-term food security and nutrition needs of refugees, internally displaced persons, and irregular migrants.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the Strengthening Early Warning Systems (SEWAA) project in leveraging Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (cGANs) for climate forecasting. The project employed a methodology that combined advanced AI with cloud computing and training sessions to enhance forecasting speed, efficiency, and accuracy. Key findings indicate that SEWAA has improved forecasting speed and efficiency, eliminated the need for expensive infrastructure, and enabled meteorological officers to acquire knowledge and skills in running, interpreting, and communicating machine learning-based forecasts. The project has also demonstrated scalability and cost-effectiveness, with the potential to transform how countries forecast and respond to extreme weather. Implications of this evaluation suggest that SEWAA can strengthen national systems, empower local expertise, and make anticipatory action the new standard in disaster risk management, with the potential for regional and global expansion.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) support to Lebanon's National Poverty Targeting Programme in addressing the country's deepening food insecurity crisis. Utilizing a retrospective analysis of programme data and contextual information, the evaluation examined the programme's impact on food security, economic stability, and poverty reduction. Key findings indicate that WFP's 10-year support has contributed to injecting liquidity into the Lebanese economy, revitalizing the local market, and reducing reliance on negative coping mechanisms among the poorest Lebanese families. However, the evaluation also highlights the need for urgent, multi-sector solutions to tackle the root causes of food insecurity, including economic instability, heavy reliance on food imports, widespread poverty, and soaring food prices. The findings suggest that sustained support to inclusive and sustainable food systems is critical to building resilience and ensuring long-term food security in Lebanon.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the WFP's Skills for Livelihood Opportunities (SLO) programme in addressing food insecurity and promoting economic empowerment among vulnerable populations, particularly women and youth, in developing countries. The evaluation employed a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative and qualitative data from various programme contexts, including rural Pakistan and refugee settings in Sudan. Key findings indicate that the SLO programme successfully provides marketable skills and support to access local job opportunities, resulting in improved skills sets (88%) and increased job prospects (81%) among programme participants, particularly women (70%). The programme's conditional transfer and additional services, such as productive equipment and financial capital, also contribute to addressing the immediate food and nutrition needs of trainees. Implications of the evaluation suggest that the SLO programme can drive national-level change by supporting policy shifts in skills development and income generation, while strengthening market actors and training institutions' quality services provision.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness and resilience of India's humanitarian system, with a focus on its preparedness, disaster risk reduction, and response to humanitarian crises. The study employed a desk review methodology, leveraging publicly available data to analyze the country's humanitarian structures, institutions, and financial mechanisms. Key findings indicate that India has a well-developed humanitarian system, characterized by a robust and effective response to saving lives, a strong and pervasive civil society response, and a self-reliant and self-sufficient humanitarian system. The country's humanitarian finance has also devolved well to address crises, and the application of technology has enabled timely assistance to victims. Furthermore, India's humanitarian system promotes innovations and good practices, with a decentralized system of federal governance and strong civil society involvement. However, the study highlights the need for further standardization and mainstreaming of civil society responses, as well as the establishment of an institutionalized coordination framework for all humanitarian actors. The evaluation's findings and recommendations are expected to benefit both the Government of India and non-government stakeholders in strengthening the humanitarian system, particularly as India assumes a more prominent global role in humanitarian action.

The evaluation objective of the Sudan Emergency Wheat Production Project is to assess the performance and results of phase one, determine how and why the results were achieved or not achieved, and provide evidence-based findings to inform operational and strategic decision-making for the World Food Programme (WFP), the African Development Bank, and other key stakeholders. The evaluation will cover the period from September 2022 to September 2025, corresponding to the duration of the project planning and implementation, and will be conducted through consultations with key stakeholders. The evaluation will build on outcome and output monitoring conducted throughout the project and will examine how well the project addressed barriers to inclusion and whether its design and implementation promoted equitable access to resources, training, and decision-making opportunities across all target groups. The evaluation team will use a range of data sources, including WFP's Annual Country Reports, project documents, and progress updates, as well as surveys and data from interviews with beneficiaries. The evaluation will be conducted by a gender, geographically, culturally, and linguistically diverse and balanced team, and will prioritize transparency, ownership, and accuracy. The evaluation findings will be shared internally within WFP and with the African Development Bank, the Government of Sudan, and other key stakeholders, with the primary goal of incorporating lessons learned into future programming and operational decision-making. The evaluation will also inform the design and implementation of phase two of the Sudan Emergency Wheat Production Project and other agriculture development projects in the wheat sector in Sudan, as well as support the development of longer-term policies and strategies to strengthen agricultural development in the wheat sector.

The evaluation objective of this project is to assess the effectiveness of the mitigation measures in place to address potential risks and ensure the social and environmental sustainability of the project. The methodology employed includes regular consultation with women, awareness-raising sessions on women's rights and economic empowerment, and the establishment of a Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) to report any incidents. Key findings indicate that women's economic empowerment is a critical aspect of the project, with risks of exploitation and violence against women being mitigated through the implementation of measures such as direct payment mechanisms and collective sales of produce. However, challenges persist, including the risk of backlash against women who challenge traditional roles and the potential for powerful men to control resources. Implications of these findings suggest that continued support and capacity-building for women-led cooperatives and SMEs are essential to ensure the project's social and environmental sustainability.

This evaluation aimed to assess the criteria and strategies driving prioritization decisions within World Food Programme (WFP) country offices during funding shortfalls. The study employed a systematic review of 42 WFP independent evaluations, covering interventions in 41 countries, to identify key patterns and findings. The analysis revealed that prioritization decisions often involve focusing on certain populations, duration and timing of assistance, or quantity and quality of WFP rations and/or transfer values. However, fluctuations in the share of unmet needs were noted, with trends differing across focus areas and crisis response and root causes. The evaluation highlighted the trade-offs between maintaining breadth of coverage and safeguarding depth of assistance to vulnerable populations, with large-sized operations being more affected by prioritization decisions. The study also noted the importance of effective communication and consultation with affected populations to mitigate potential negative impacts of prioritization decisions. The findings have implications for WFP's operational and strategic planning, emphasizing the need for transparent and evidence-based prioritization decisions that balance competing demands and minimize negative consequences for beneficiaries.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) targeting approaches in emergency responses. The evaluation objective was to identify evidence gaps and areas for improvement in WFP's targeting practices, including vulnerability and needs assessments, contextual and programmatic relevance, and capacity to conduct needs assessments and implement targeting according to WFP standards. 

The evaluation methodology involved a review of 23 evaluation reports from 54 evaluations of WFP country strategic plans, corporate emergency responses, policies, and strategic areas, conducted between 2021 and 2023. The key findings indicate significant evidence gaps in all evaluations reviewed, particularly in the areas of quality and relevance of vulnerability and needs assessments, contextual and programmatic relevance of targeting methods, and capacity to conduct needs assessments and implement targeting according to WFP standards. The gaps were attributed to limited guidance on evaluating targeting, a lack of formal documentation on assessments and targeting, high staff turnover in emergencies, and serious gaps in monitoring.

The evaluation highlights the importance of contextual and programmatic relevance, advantages, and risks of targeting methods used, as well as the application of corporate and country-specific strategies, guidelines, and standard operating procedures on targeting. It also emphasizes the need for capacity strengthening, particularly in the transfer of digital technologies and data, and the protection of sensitive personal identifying information. The evaluation recommends strengthening monitoring and verification of targeting effectiveness, giving greater attention to inclusion of the most vulnerable groups, and improving the quality and relevance of vulnerability and needs assessments.

The implications of these findings suggest that WFP needs to improve its guidance on evaluating targeting, enhance its capacity to conduct needs assessments and implement targeting according to WFP standards, and strengthen its monitoring and verification of targeting effectiveness. Additionally, WFP should prioritize the inclusion of the most vulnerable groups and improve the quality and relevance of vulnerability and needs assessments to ensure that its targeting approaches are effective and equitable.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the USDA Local and Regional Food Aid Procurement (LRP) Program in supporting the transition of school meals programs from World Food Programme (WFP) management to host governments or local communities. The evaluation methodology involved a systematic review of 15 WFP-commissioned independent evaluations of LRP components under McGovern-Dole programs in five countries (Cambodia, Kenya, Laos, Rwanda, and Nepal) between 2017 and 2024. Key findings indicate that a progressive, phased approach to transition is crucial, and sustained support from WFP is needed post-transition to strengthen systems, refine procurement and pricing processes, and build monitoring and quality control capacities of governments. The evaluation also highlights the importance of localized needs assessments, adaptive management, and strong monitoring, evaluation, and knowledge management systems for ensuring sustainable outcomes. However, shifts in government leadership can reverse or stall progress, and the duration of LRP projects is often too short to ensure sustainable transition and inter-ministerial coordination. The evaluation concludes that LRP demonstrates potential for strong efficiency and can serve as a strong introductory model for transitioning schools to manage purchases themselves, but more intentional efforts are needed to ensure gender equality and women's empowerment is embedded from the outset in LFP designs.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) climate action programming, with a focus on integration, coherence, and forward-looking climate analysis. The evaluation employed a mixed-methods approach, analyzing data from 24 countries where WFP interventions were implemented. Key findings indicate that while WFP's climate action has led to positive outcomes at various levels, including livelihood diversification, food security, and risk reduction, challenges remain in achieving lasting resilience and systemic change. Integrated climate action programming that combines short-term adaptation with long-term transformative actions is more successful than stand-alone interventions. Participation and capacity building of national and local institutions, as well as community engagement, are critical factors of successful climate action programmes. However, further evidence is needed on the potential for leveraging private sector involvement and the role of non-governmental organizations (NGOs) in enhancing effectiveness. Additionally, there is a need for more evidence on the best practices for inter-agency collaboration on climate action, particularly on how to overcome competition for funds and coordinate joint actions more effectively. The evaluation also highlights the importance of strengthening monitoring and evaluation systems to inform future climate programming and policy development.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) budget revision processes in supporting timely and strategic programming adaptations. The evaluation methodology involved a systematic review of 21 WFP-commissioned independent evaluations, which were rated satisfactory or above by an external post-hoc quality assessment. Key findings indicate that budget revisions can be time-consuming and may require significant human resource investments, potentially hindering WFP's ability to respond promptly to emergencies. However, the evaluation also highlights the importance of budget revisions as an effective tool for programming adaptation, enabling WFP to adjust its programming and respond to changes in needs. The analysis reveals that, between 2018 and 2021, WFP processed 332 budget revisions for 87 country offices, averaging approximately one revision per year per office. The evaluation suggests that proactive communication efforts are necessary to enhance the visibility of strategic changes introduced by budget revisions to non-WFP country stakeholders. Overall, the findings support the recommendation to ensure that crisis response placeholders are included in Country Strategic Plans to facilitate timely responses to emergencies.

The evaluation objective of the Joint Project is to assess the effectiveness of the social protection interventions in enhancing the coverage of national social protection programmes, building resilience, and promoting inclusive, shock-responsive, and nutrition-sensitive national social protection systems in the Sahel region. 

The Joint Project employs a twin-track approach, channeling resources directly through national systems or, when these are overstretched or constrained, through partners, in alignment with national programmes. This approach has enabled the expansion of social protection programme coverage, reaching over 3.3 million people across five countries (Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali, Mauritania, and Niger) through cash transfers and complementary services. 

Key findings include the establishment of a strong partnership with the World Bank in the Sahel, the development of joint analyses and diagnostics on adaptive social protection, and the dissemination of standards for main pillars and instruments of adaptive social protection. The Joint Project has also supported the set-up of permanent national social safety programmes that can reach scale, with a focus on building capacities among country leadership and governments. 

The implications of the Joint Project's findings and outcomes are significant, as they contribute to the development and consolidation of national safety net programmes that address structural drivers of poverty and chronic vulnerability. The project's approach has the potential to elevate social protection as a vital component in addressing chronic needs in a more sustainable and cost-effective fashion, moving beyond humanitarian assistance alone.

This evaluation aimed to assess the feasibility of shifting Cambodia's dietary patterns towards healthier and more sustainable options, while mitigating the triple burden of malnutrition and environmental impacts. To achieve this objective, a multi-objective linear optimization model was applied using the WFP Enhance platform, which considered energy and nutrient needs, diversity recommendations, cost minimization, and environmental impact reduction. The analysis revealed that a shift towards a healthy dietary pattern can lower greenhouse gas emissions by up to 31 percent and reduce the water footprint by up to 32 percent. Fortified rice was identified as a cost-effective solution to address micronutrient deficiencies, particularly for low-income households. Climate-smart production practices in the rice and livestock sectors can also contribute to reducing emissions. However, significant changes are required to overcome supply and demand barriers, including increasing fruit and vegetable production, improving value chains, and promoting social behavior change. The findings highlight the importance of staple food fortification, particularly for the poorest households, and the need for a strong focus on increasing production and improving value chains for fruit and vegetables. The analysis suggests that a combination of dietary shifts, climate-smart production practices, and staple food fortification can have a substantial impact on reducing the triple burden of malnutrition and environmental impacts in Cambodia.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) response to the humanitarian crisis in Niger, with a focus on ensuring the sustainability of investments and the delivery of life-saving assistance. The evaluation employed a systems-based approach, examining WFP's capacity to rapidly scale up humanitarian operations, deliver cash assistance, and implement integrated resilience-building programmes. Key findings indicate that WFP's flagship programme has delivered tangible results, supporting longer-term reductions in humanitarian needs and contributing to community-led peace-building efforts. However, the suspension of international budget support to Niger is likely to have a negative impact on economic development and access to basic services. The evaluation highlights the importance of sustained investments in Niger's social protection system, particularly in the context of ongoing climate change and climatic shocks. The findings also emphasize the need for a coordinated and targeted review of humanitarian assistance and multi-sectoral development responses, taking into account the evolving needs of the population, including specific needs of pastoralists and vulnerable groups. The evaluation concludes that demonstrating the multiple benefits of resilience programmes, including in terms of reducing humanitarian needs in times of shock, will strengthen advocacy efforts for sustainable and diversified financing mechanisms.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the International Aid System (IASC) members' collective efforts in responding to the humanitarian crisis in Ukraine, particularly in addressing the needs of the most vulnerable populations. The evaluation methodology involved a comprehensive review of existing evaluation reports and evidence. Key findings indicate that the collective humanitarian response in Ukraine was largely relevant in addressing the immediate needs of affected populations, with operational effectiveness characterized by rapid expansion, flexible funding, and strong operational leadership. However, the response was also marked by challenges in scale and coherence, with protection interventions not always aligned across humanitarian actors. Furthermore, capacity-strengthening efforts were fragmented, and opportunities to integrate humanitarian aid into national systems were often overlooked, restricting coherence and sustainability. The evaluation also highlights the importance of leveraging national capacities, including local actors and partnerships, to deliver assistance to affected people. The findings suggest that the response was more effective in meeting immediate needs than in enabling strategic transition, resilience, or sustainable outcomes. The implications of this evaluation are that humanitarian actors should prioritize more coordinated and strategic engagement with national actors, and that opportunities remain to further embed and expand nationally led mechanisms to ensure more inclusive, accountable, and context-driven coordination structures.

This evaluation aims to assess the effectiveness of the Tanzania Food Trade for the Advancement of Microfinance (FTMA) programme in strengthening inclusive markets and partnerships for sustainable food systems. To achieve this objective, the evaluation will apply the United Nations Evaluation Group (UNEG) and OECD/DAC evaluation criteria of relevance, coherence, efficiency, effectiveness, impact, and sustainability. The evaluation will assess the programme's design, implementation, and outcomes across four pillars and actors, including smallholder farmers, financial service companies, and market players. Key findings will inform programme improvements, adaptive management, and the potential design of Phase III, while also supporting advocacy efforts and policy reforms. The evaluation will examine the programme's contributions to smallholder farmers, stakeholders, and value chain actors, and identify risks to programme implementation, success, local ownership, and sustainability. The evaluation results will be shared with stakeholders and donors for accountability and learning, and will inform the World Food Programme (WFP) Tanzania Country Strategic Plan (CSP 2022-2027).

This evaluation aimed to assess the impact of climate-related disasters and the effectiveness of climate action in mitigating their effects. The study employed a review of existing literature, including the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) assessment reports and the Aon Weather, Climate and Catastrophe Insight, 2022. Key findings indicate that climate-related disasters have resulted in significant economic losses, with 2021 being the third-costliest year on record, and have caused widespread disruption, particularly in vulnerable communities. The evaluation also highlights that the world is underinvesting in climate action, with climate finance failing to reach areas where losses and damages outpace the capabilities of governments and the international aid system. Furthermore, the study reveals that food productivity growth has declined by 21 percent due to global heating, and that the failure to address climate action is considered the most severe risk in the medium and long term. The evaluation concludes that transformative action is necessary to address the inequitable and unsustainable nature of food systems, and that effective and scalable solutions, such as those promoted by the World Food Programme (WFP), are essential to help vulnerable communities prepare for, respond to, and recover from climate shocks and stresses.

This evaluation aimed to understand the causes and consequences of the 2021-2023 food price inflation surge on food security and nutrition. The study employed a quantitative methodology, utilizing data from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the World Bank, to analyze the relationship between food price inflation and food insecurity. Key findings indicate that while food price inflation has detrimental effects, GDP appears to be a stronger factor in determining food insecurity. The study also found that food price inflation has risen significantly since late 2020, peaking in January 2023, and that the prevalence of food insecurity has remained consistently higher in rural areas than in urban areas since 2022. Furthermore, the study suggests that most countries are either off-track or lack sufficient data to achieve the 2030 Global Nutrition Targets. The implications of these findings highlight the need for policymakers to address the root causes of food price inflation and to prioritize strategies that promote economic growth and reduce poverty.

This evaluation aimed to shed light on the complex food systems in the Amazon region, understanding their dynamics, key actors, and the challenges they face. To achieve this objective, a mixed-methods approach was employed, combining bottom-up and top-down methods to integrate local experiences with academic trends. The study examined the predominant narratives on Amazonian food systems, key concepts, and actors involved, as well as the dynamics that affect them. Key findings include the importance of indigenous communities' knowledge and sustainable management practices, the impact of extractive industries and industrial agriculture on local ecosystems, and the need to prioritize food security and nutrition, social aspects, productive and environmental aspects, and economic and governance aspects. The evaluation also identified five types of dynamics that influence Amazonian food systems: demographics, technology, markets, climate, and politics. The study highlights the need to understand these interactions to develop strategies that promote more sustainable, inclusive, and resilient food systems. The findings suggest that local knowledge systems, including indigenous communities, offer sustainable and accessible solutions, but are often marginalized in research and policy. The evaluation concludes that ensuring the resilience of Amazonian food systems is crucial for the livelihoods of present and future generations, and that a comprehensive understanding of the region's food systems is essential for devising effective solutions.

This evaluation aimed to assess the impact of school health and nutrition (SHN) programs on improving learning outcomes, inclusive education systems, and contributing to the achievement of the nutrition, health, gender equality, and wider Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The evaluation employed a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative data from various studies and reports with qualitative insights from global agencies and experts. Key findings indicate that SHN programs have a significant impact on fostering equity in and through schools, particularly for girls and children at risk of exclusion. These programs can lead to improved learning outcomes, increased enrollment and attendance rates, and reduced absenteeism due to health-related issues. Specifically, interventions such as school meals, health services, hand-washing promotion, and comprehensive sexuality education have been shown to have positive effects on health and education outcomes. For instance, school meals can increase enrollment rates by 9% on average and reduce anaemia in adolescent girls by up to 20%. Similarly, comprehensive sexuality education can promote sexual and reproductive health and rights, and improve sexual and reproductive health outcomes. The evaluation highlights the importance of prioritizing the health and wellbeing of children in school as a sound economic and social investment. It also emphasizes the need to address the significant gaps in quality, content, and access to school health and nutrition programs, particularly in low-income countries. The evaluation concludes that investing in SHN programs is crucial for achieving the SDGs, particularly in fragile and conflict-affected areas and refugee settings.

This evaluation aimed to assess the potential contribution of school meals programmes to peace and social cohesion in fragile and conflict-affected settings. The study employed a qualitative methodology, drawing on existing literature and case studies to explore the pathways of change through which school meals may contribute to positive outcomes. Key findings suggest that school meals can foster improved social cohesion, equitable access to basic services, and safeguard continued investments in human capital development. However, the evidence on school meals in emergencies and their contribution to peace and social cohesion is limited, and more research is needed to understand the impact of school meals on these outcomes. The study also highlights the importance of conflict sensitivity, equity, and inclusivity in school meals programming to ensure that it contributes to peace and social cohesion. The evaluation's implications suggest that school meals programmes can be a strategic tool for fostering contributions to peace and social cohesion, but their design and delivery must be carefully considered to maximize their potential impact.

This evaluation aimed to assess the role of clean energy in food value chains, with a focus on identifying key services, barriers, and programmatic entry points for sustainable impact. The methodology involved analyzing the opportunities and risks of various energy solutions, understanding the enabling environment and socio-cultural context, and identifying external supporting interventions to enable sustainable functioning. Key findings include the fundamental obstacle of limited energy access in rural areas, which hinders agricultural productivity, food security, and resilience. Investing in sustainable energy, particularly solar, can transform rural economies by creating youth employment and making farming more viable. Energy access is essential to increase production, reduce post-harvest losses, improve market access, and build food security and resilience. However, energy gaps and barriers, such as low purchasing power, poor infrastructure, and lack of awareness, prevent energy value chains from being functional and effective in delivering energy services to end users. Addressing these barriers through supporting interventions, such as building energy market systems and promoting market-based approaches, is a long-term, sustainable alternative to creating artificial delivery activities. The evaluation highlights the importance of understanding the enabling environment, socio-cultural factors, and external supporting interventions to ensure the sustainable functioning of energy services in food value chains.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the distribution of iron-fortified rice through social protection programmes in addressing iron deficiency and preventing anaemia in the Philippines. The evaluation methodology involved a review of existing initiatives, including the partnership between the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) and the National Nutrition Council (NNC) to implement large-scale rice fortification, as well as the launch of the Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition (PPAN) 2023-2028. Key findings included the successful institutionalization of fortified foods in school meals programmes, the introduction of multiple micronutrient-fortified rice kernels through pilot projects, and the commitment of WFP to support the Government in ensuring accessible fortified rice through nutrition-sensitive interventions and commercial channels. The evaluation also highlighted the importance of social and behaviour change (SBC) as a strategic pillar of the PPAN, with a focus on inclusion and evidence generation from local communities. Implications of the evaluation include the need for strict adherence to laws and policies on rice fortification, the development of a monitoring system for rice fortification, and the commercialization of iron-fortified rice through the establishment of blending facilities and the involvement of farmers.

This evaluation aimed to assess the affordability of a nutrient-adequate diet in Timor-Leste, with a focus on understanding the nutritional status and well-being of the population. The analysis employed the Cost of the Diet (CotD) methodology, which utilizes linear programming to estimate the lowest-cost nutrient-adequate basket based on food prices and availability. Key findings indicate that the national average cost of a nutrient-adequate diet is US$10.09 per household of five members per day, with significant regional variations, ranging from US$7.15 in Aileu to US$13.91 in Covalima. The analysis also highlights the limited availability of nutritious foods, particularly iron-rich items, in certain municipalities, which hinders the estimation of the cost of the nutrient-adequate basket. The evaluation's implications suggest that a household of five members would need to spend approximately US$300 per month to cover their nutrient needs, underscoring the challenges faced by households in affording a nutritious diet amidst high food prices and reduced purchasing power. The analysis is subject to limitations, including the lack of recent population expenditure data, which precludes a comprehensive assessment of non-affordability.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of various methods for preparing and processing sanan (a type of plant-based food) in a blender. The methodology involved comparing different techniques, including the use of ahi-matan (heat), liis-mutin (cold), and fehuk-ropa (a type of paste), to determine the optimal approach for achieving a smooth and consistent texture. Key findings indicate that the use of ahi-matan and liis-mutin in combination with a blender resulted in a smooth and creamy texture, while the addition of fehuk-ropa improved the overall consistency. The results also suggest that the use of a blender with a high-speed setting and a suitable container size is essential for achieving the desired texture. The implications of these findings are that cooks and food processors can use these methods to prepare sanan with a smooth and consistent texture, which can enhance the overall quality and palatability of the dish.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) assistance in supporting refugees in Türkiye. The methodology involved a comprehensive needs assessment of refugees living in seven camps, excluding those hosting Ukrainian refugees, as well as an analysis of the impact of WFP's e-voucher assistance programme. Key findings indicate that one-third of surveyed households are highly vulnerable, with half relying on WFP assistance as their primary source of income, and the majority lacking plans to leave the camps. Notably, households headed by women are more likely to resort to coping behaviours. The evaluation also highlights the significance of the e-voucher assistance in ensuring refugees' access to sufficient food, promoting a healthy and diverse diet, and reducing negative coping behaviours, while enhancing Türkiye's national crisis-response capacities.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the Social Safety Net (SSN) transfer value in addressing needs and vulnerability levels among the target population. The assessment was initiated in Q4 2022, but its progress was interrupted by the earthquakes in early 2023. Utilizing a mixed-methods approach, the evaluation collected quantitative data in September, which will be complemented by qualitative data through focus group discussions and key informant interviews. The findings of this analysis will be discussed collaboratively among stakeholders in Q4 to inform programme design and targeting options, ensuring that assistance is provided to the right people at the right time.

This evaluation aims to assess the effectiveness of the United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS) in providing reliable and vital air transport services to support global humanitarian action. The evaluation methodology involved analyzing key performance indicators, including the number of passengers and cargo transported, and the number of humanitarian workers supported. Key findings indicate that UNHAS has been instrumental in responding to emergency situations, enabling the rapid deployment of helicopters for medical evacuations and security relocations. Over the past two decades, UNHAS has evolved into the backbone of humanitarian access, flying in and out of some of the world's most dangerous and remote locations. In 2024, UNHAS transported over 3.8 million humanitarian workers to communities in need in over 33 countries, bringing hope to vulnerable families affected by violence or climate extremes. The evaluation also highlights UNHAS's commitment to sustainability, with the organization taking decisive steps toward pioneering the use of sustainable aviation fuels in humanitarian aviation operations. The implications of these findings suggest that UNHAS remains essential to support the safe, efficient, and effective transport of humanitarian assistance to hard-to-reach areas, particularly in contexts of high humanitarian needs and significant access constraints.

This evaluation aimed to assess the humanitarian situation in Chad, with a focus on the refugee crisis and logistical challenges. The methodology involved analyzing data from the 2024 Humanitarian Response Plan and reports from the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and the International Organization for Migration (IOM). Key findings indicate that Chad hosts a significant refugee population, with an estimated 1,215,631 refugees as of August 2024, and 1,043,143 Sudanese refugees since April 2023. The country's infrastructure poses significant logistical challenges, including unpaved roads that become impassable during the rainy season and limited air transportation options. However, the introduction of a new helicopter and a Dash 8-103 aircraft to the UNHAS fleet is expected to enhance the country's humanitarian response capacity. The implications of these findings suggest that the humanitarian community must prioritize addressing the refugee crisis and improving logistical infrastructure to effectively respond to the needs of vulnerable populations in Chad.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) humanitarian food assistance initiatives in India and their potential for scaling up nationwide. The evaluation methodology involved analyzing the outcomes of various WFP projects, including the provision of food assistance to Afghanistan, supply chain optimization, and capacity building of school cooks and helpers. Key findings include the successful completion of the supply chain optimization project in 13 out of 31 designated states, the training of 100,000 school cooks in Odisha using the FoSafMDM app, and the scaling up of the intervention in Rajasthan. Additionally, the evaluation highlighted the development of a model allowing 12 drought-prone states to request funding from the National Disaster Mitigation Fund and the launch of the Solar 4 Resilience initiative in Odisha. The implications of these findings suggest that WFP's initiatives have the potential to improve food security and resilience in vulnerable communities, and that scaling up these initiatives nationwide could have significant benefits for food-insecure populations.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) partnership with the Government of India in promoting climate-resilient millets, improving maternal and child nutrition, and enhancing food security. The evaluation employed a mixed-methods approach, combining data from various sources, including project reports, stakeholder interviews, and field observations. Key findings indicate that the partnership has led to the promotion of climate-resilient millets in tribal areas of Odisha, the production and distribution of fortified blended foods for the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme, and the installation of mobile storage units (MSUs) in remote and hilly areas. The evaluation also highlights the development of smart warehouses, which utilize Internet of Things (IoT) devices and data analytics to optimize food grain management. Furthermore, the partnership has supported the integration of fortified staples through the Take-Home Ration (THR) and hot cooked meals under food safety net schemes. The implications of these findings suggest that the partnership has the potential to improve food security, enhance nutrition outcomes, and promote sustainable agriculture practices in India.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS) in supporting the global response to the COVID-19 pandemic and other humanitarian crises. The evaluation employed a qualitative methodology, examining UNHAS operations in various countries, including Afghanistan, Cameroon, Chad, Guinea, Libya, Mali, Sudan, Syria, and Yemen. Key findings indicate that UNHAS has continued to provide critical air transport services, facilitating the movement of humanitarian workers, medical personnel, and life-saving supplies to remote and challenging locations. Despite the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic, UNHAS operations have maintained a high level of reliability and safety, transporting over 2.5 million passengers since 2013. The evaluation highlights the importance of UNHAS in enabling humanitarian access to populations in need of assistance, particularly in areas affected by physical constraints, insecurity, and administrative obstacles. The implications of this evaluation are that UNHAS continues to play a pivotal role in supporting humanitarian responses, and its services are essential for the delivery of life-saving assistance to crisis-affected populations. However, the evaluation also notes that UNHAS is facing a critical funding situation, threatening the sustainability of its operations.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS) in providing timely and unhindered access to crisis-affected locations. The evaluation methodology involved analyzing UNHAS operations in various countries, including Burkina Faso, Mozambique, the Syrian Arab Republic, and others, where UNHAS played a crucial role in delivering humanitarian assistance. Key findings indicate that UNHAS operations have been essential in enabling access to hard-to-reach locations, particularly in areas with increased humanitarian needs, insecurity, and access restrictions. The service has continued to operate uninterrupted, despite challenges posed by COVID-19-related restrictions, and has expanded its services to include helicopter operations in remote areas. The evaluation highlights the critical role of UNHAS in providing a safe, effective, and efficient air service for the humanitarian community, particularly in countries with limited commercial air connections. The implications of this evaluation are that timely and adequate funding is necessary for UNHAS to continue operating, and that the service's sustainability is crucial for maintaining humanitarian access and response efforts in crisis-affected areas.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) Country-Led CSPs in promoting sustainable food systems. The evaluation objective was to identify opportunities to improve agricultural practices, strengthen supply chains, and ensure access to nutritious food for vulnerable populations. The methodology involved examining the interactions between production, distribution, and consumption in food systems, as well as the role of strategic interventions in these interconnected domains. Key findings included the potential for improved sustainability in food systems to generate benefits beyond production and distribution, such as improved nutritional outcomes and human health. The evaluation also highlighted the importance of infrastructure investments, including transportation facilities and cold storage, in reducing post-harvest losses and improving the efficient distribution of food products. Furthermore, the analysis identified synergies between food supply, infrastructure, and social development, which can contribute to a more stable development trajectory and reduce reliance on emergency support. The implications of these findings suggest that WFP's interventions can have a positive impact on food system sustainability, livelihoods, and resilience, ultimately contributing to improved food diversity, livelihoods, and resilience in the face of various challenges.

This evaluation aimed to assess the potential of digital payments to enhance social assistance delivery and promote digital financial inclusion in Barbados. The study employed a mixed-methods approach, combining key informant interviews, focus groups, and workshops with beneficiaries, financial regulators, and institutions to analyze the digital financial ecosystem and identify practical ways to strengthen social protection. Key findings include the growing demand for digital merchant solutions, the need for inclusive practices to expand access to financial services, and the importance of digital financial literacy to ensure effective use of financial services. The study also highlighted the challenges faced by vulnerable groups in accessing and using digital payment solutions, including low merchant acceptance, limited integration with commercial banks, and limited options for physical cash-in and cash withdrawals. The evaluation's implications suggest that investing in strategic public-private partnerships and strengthening the integration between non-traditional financial service providers and the formal banking system are critical to building a more inclusive financial ecosystem. Furthermore, the study emphasizes the need for broader adoption of inclusive practices, such as low-cost merchant payment solutions, to ensure that all financial services, both traditional and digital, can work seamlessly together to enhance the accessibility and efficiency of social assistance payments.

The evaluation objective of this review is to assess the World Food Programme's (WFP) financial and budgetary situation, particularly in light of the decreased contribution forecast for 2025. The methodology employed involves analyzing the WFP management plan for 2025-2027, considering the updated contribution forecast, and reviewing the projected operational requirements and cost-saving measures implemented by the Executive Director. Key findings include a decreased contribution forecast from USD 8 billion to USD 6.4 billion, projected operational requirements of USD 19.1 billion, and cost-saving measures aimed at reducing the programme support and administrative appropriation by up to 10 percent. The implications of these findings are that WFP will need to reassess its resource mobilization strategy, prioritize its funding sources, and implement measures to stabilize its workforce in response to the evolving funding landscape.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme (WFP) Centre of Excellence (CoE) against Hunger in Brazil's technical assistance and capacity strengthening programme in development contexts for Africa, Asia, and Latin America. The evaluation employed a demand-driven approach, consistent with the Centre's methodology, to support countries in engaging in South-South cooperation within a broader programmatic and development context. Key findings indicate that the WFP CoE has successfully supported over 30 countries in developing their capacities, engaging with over 80 countries worldwide, and benefiting more than 4 million school-going children and thousands of smallholder farmers participating in home-grown school feeding (HGSF) programmes. The evaluation highlights the Centre's ability to respond to capacity gaps identified through an assessment process led by the partner government, providing nationally-tailored strengthened government capacities in policies and legislation frameworks, institutional capacity and coordination, strategic planning, national programme design, and engagement and participation of local communities. The evaluation also underscores the importance of the WFP CoE's Virtual Exchanges, a modality of remote assistance tailored for WFP Country Offices and governments to produce results and achieve outcomes on SDG 2 as needed by each national context. The findings suggest that the WFP CoE's remote support, including Virtual Exchanges, has been effective in minimizing the need for physical presence, allowing for quick responses to country demands, and promoting partnership scoping and knowledge mobilization across 13 programme focus areas. The evaluation's implications suggest that the WFP CoE's approach can be scaled up to support more countries in achieving SDG 2 – Zero Hunger, and that the Centre's methodology and tools can be adapted to meet the evolving needs of countries in the context of the digital transformation.

This evaluation aimed to assess the global food insecurity situation as of June 2025. The methodology involved analyzing data from 67 countries where the World Food Programme (WFP) operates and where data was available. Key findings indicate a decrease in the number of people facing acute food insecurity from 343 million in 74 countries, as reported in the November 2024 Global Outlook, to 319 million in the current mid-year update. However, this decrease is attributed to the lack of updated data in seven countries, rather than an actual improvement in the food insecurity situation. The implications of this evaluation suggest that the reported decrease may not accurately reflect the true extent of food insecurity globally.

This evaluation aimed to assess the impact of flexible funding on the World Food Programme's (WFP) capacity to respond to humanitarian crises. The evaluation methodology involved analyzing data on flexible funding contributions from various partners, as well as case studies of successful flexible funding initiatives. Key findings indicate that flexible funding enabled WFP to scale up assistance in crisis-affected areas, such as Lebanon and Chad, and to deliver principled humanitarian assistance at scale over time. The evaluation also highlights the importance of flexible funding in enabling WFP to respond with speed and agility, particularly in a world of escalating humanitarian needs. The implications of this evaluation are that flexible funding is critical to WFP's capacity to respond to emergencies and provide life-saving assistance to those who need it most, and that partners should continue to invest in flexible funding to support WFP's efforts to strengthen resilience and help people back on track after a disaster has hit.

The evaluation objective of the World Food Programme (WFP) in 2024 was to assess its efforts in addressing hunger and building resilience in communities affected by conflict, climate change, and poverty. The evaluation methodology involved analyzing WFP's global operations, partnerships, and funding strategies to identify key achievements and challenges. 

Key findings of the evaluation include WFP's significant expansion of emergency operations in Sudan, Haiti, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, reaching over 1.3 million people with food assistance. The organization also strengthened its partnerships with governments, NGOs, companies, and foundations to enhance national social protection and nutrition programs. WFP's innovative use of technology, such as blockchain-based systems, enabled efficient and rapid response to emergencies. Furthermore, the organization continued to prioritize school meals and nutrition programs, reaching over 150 million children worldwide. 

The implications of these findings are that WFP's efforts have made a tangible impact in addressing hunger and building resilience in communities affected by crisis. However, the organization faces significant funding challenges, with a decline in flexible funding contributing to difficulties in planning and responding to emergencies. To address these challenges, WFP must continue to be agile and innovative in adapting to changing circumstances, embracing new technologies and partnerships, and pursuing every viable funding option to deliver full value for money for its donors.

This evaluation aimed to assess the purchasing power of households in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, by examining the cost of a food basket and the terms of trade (ToT) indicator. The methodology involved collecting market prices of food items from the Department of Agricultural Marketing (DAM) and calculating the cost of a food basket per person per month at the national level. The study found that the food basket value did not vary significantly across sub-districts, with the basket value of Ukhiya, the largest makeshift camp, serving as the base. The purchasing power of households was calculated by measuring the ratio of the average wage rate of unskilled labourers to the average retail price of rice, indicating the amount of rice unskilled workers can purchase with their daily wage. Key findings include a 6 percent increase in retail prices in December 2022, but a 14 percent decrease year-on-year, and a purchasing power ratio of approximately 1,600 kg of rice with a day's wage in January 2023. The implications of these findings suggest that the purchasing power of households in Cox's Bazar may be influenced by fluctuations in food prices and wage rates, highlighting the need for continued monitoring of these indicators to inform humanitarian response efforts.

This evaluation aimed to assess the food security situation in Bangladesh, with a focus on the impact of income shocks and seasonality on households' ability to access nutritious food. The study employed a mixed-methods approach, utilizing a survey to collect data on households' food consumption scores, livelihood coping mechanisms, income sources, and income changes due to shocks. Key findings indicate that low-income households (30%) were more likely to be food insecure compared to medium-income (8%) and high-income households (3%). The prevalence of food insecurity was particularly high in low-income households with members having disabilities. The survey revealed that 43% of households purchased food on credit, 22% reduced expenses on health, and 13% spent their savings due to income loss and recurrent shocks. Furthermore, the study found that households with disabilities were more food insecure, and the seasonality of income opportunities and multiple shocks severely affected households' ability to access nutritious food. The results also highlighted the inadequate diet of households, with 40% of low-income households having a poor diet, and only 13% of households consuming iron-rich food regularly. The evaluation suggests that food and fuel price shocks were incredibly costly for low-income households, and a detailed disaggregated survey is necessary to investigate the root causes of food insecurity in different geographic locations.

This evaluation aimed to assess the functionality of markets in Bhasan Char, a designated resettlement area for Rohingya refugees, to ensure the community's food security and economic well-being are adequately supported. The methodology involved data collection through surveys and observations of traders and market dynamics. Key findings indicate that the market infrastructure is hindered by poor conditions, particularly during the rainy season, and that traders lack knowledge in bookkeeping and inventory management. Furthermore, the supply chain is vulnerable to risks such as scarcity of basic food items, monopoly risks, and limited availability of large boats for transportation. The evaluation also highlights the limited financial services and infrastructure available to refugees, restricting their access to cash and income-generating opportunities. The results suggest that the market's functionality is at moderate to high risk, with potential implications for the economic well-being and food security of the Rohingya refugee community.

This evaluation aimed to assess the impact of global food price shocks on food security in Cambodia. The evaluation employed a market monitoring methodology, collecting data on food prices and market functionality from 56 monitored markets across the country. Key findings indicate that the cost of the World Food Programme's (WFP) basic food basket (BFB) experienced a moderate decline of 3.6% in December 2023, reducing it to USD 27.3 per person per month. However, the BFB cost remained 2.9% higher than the same month in the previous year due to higher prices for some key commodities, particularly mixed rice. The evaluation also notes that the global rice prices are projected to increase by 6% in 2024, following a 28% rise in 2023, driven by increased demand and reduced supply. The findings suggest that the rising price of rice, coupled with favorable weather conditions, led to an increase in paddy cultivation and production in 2023. The evaluation's implications highlight the need for continued monitoring of food prices and market functionality to inform policy decisions and mitigate the impact of global food price shocks on food security in Cambodia.

This evaluation aimed to assess the impact of global food and energy market shocks on food availability and access to markets in Cambodia. The study employed a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative data from the World Food Programme (WFP) and the Agricultural Marketing Office (AMO) with qualitative insights from market chiefs and traders. Key findings indicate that the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict, coupled with the COVID-19 pandemic and a global economic slowdown, has led to significant price increases in essential food items, particularly grains and fertilizers. The global FAO Food Price Index (FFPI) has been on a downward trend, but the price of diesel remains high, potentially affecting food production and prices. Moreover, the global economic slowdown, projected at 2.7% for 2023, will likely lead to dampened economic growth in Cambodia, exacerbating the food crisis. The study also highlights the importance of access to fertilizer as a major challenge over the coming months, with potential profound impacts on global food production. The evaluation's findings have significant implications for policymakers and stakeholders, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions to mitigate the effects of these shocks on food availability and access to markets in Cambodia.

This evaluation aimed to assess the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, Russia-Ukraine war, and global economic shocks on food availability and access to markets in Cambodia. The methodology involved monitoring retail and wholesale prices of key food items, assessing market functionality, and interviewing market chiefs to evaluate supply and demand issues. Key findings indicate that the global food crisis has been partially aggravated by the Russia-Ukraine war, resulting in rising global food prices, particularly for wheat, maize, and rice. The price of diesel remained relatively high, which may negatively affect food production and prices. In contrast, the price of gasoline decreased. The evaluation also found that Cambodia's largest trading partners, the US and China, are experiencing a cyclical economic slowdown, which will dampen economic growth in Cambodia. The main challenge over the coming months will be access to fertilizer, as global fertilizer prices remain high. This is likely to have a profound impact on global food production, with rice production in 2022/2023 expected to decrease by 2.4% compared to 2021. The implications of these shocks are significant, with 19 countries having instigated food export bans and 8 countries implementing export-limiting measures.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) response to the humanitarian crisis in the Northwest and Southwest regions of Cameroon, where ongoing conflict between State Security Forces and Non-State Armed Groups has resulted in a severe food insecurity situation. Utilizing the Cadre Harmonisé results, the evaluation methodology involved analyzing the impact of WFP's assistance activities, implemented within the framework of the WFP Country Strategic Plan (2022-2026), on the food security of affected populations. Key findings indicate that, despite a six percent decrease in severely food-insecure individuals compared to 2024, approximately 613,250 people in the region are expected to face severe food insecurity between June and August 2025, with the Northwest region accounting for two-thirds of the affected population. The evaluation highlights WFP's efforts to promote respect, dignity, protection, and accountability to affected people through its interventions, including the establishment of a call centre and the implementation of locally-sourced food assistance programmes that support local producers and enhance food systems in the communities. The evaluation's implications suggest that continued support is necessary to address the ongoing humanitarian crisis and to further develop the food systems in the affected regions.

This evaluation aimed to assess the humanitarian situation in Cameroon, focusing on the impact of the non-state armed groups' insurgencies in the Lake Chad Basin and the Ukraine crisis on food insecurity and malnutrition. The evaluation employed a mixed-methods approach, utilizing data from the Cadre Harmonisé, SMART1 nutrition surveys, and other sources to analyze the situation. Key findings indicate that the Far North Region is experiencing severe food insecurity, with approximately 701,000 people severely food-insecure between January and May 2023, and a projected 322,600 food-insecure people between June and August 2023. The region also has persistently high rates of malnutrition, with a global acute malnutrition (GAM) rate of 8.0 percent. The evaluation highlights the need for continued humanitarian assistance, particularly in the face of increasing humanitarian access challenges. The World Food Programme (WFP) is responding to the crisis, but faces a significant funding shortfall, with a 66 percent funding gap for the period from May to October 2023. The evaluation emphasizes the importance of incorporating cross-cutting themes, including gender, protection, climate-friendly interventions, and resilience-building, into humanitarian interventions. Ultimately, the evaluation aims to inform the development of an adaptive and shock-responsive social protection system in collaboration with the Government of Cameroon.

This evaluation aims to assess the effectiveness of the WFP Centre of Excellence against Hunger Brazil in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) and SDG 17 (strengthen the means of implementation and revitalise partnerships). The Centre has employed a methodology of trilateral South-South cooperation, technical assistance, and advisory services to support countries in achieving their development goals. Key findings include the expansion of partnerships, the successful implementation of school feeding programs, and the development of capacity-building initiatives for national governments. The Centre's work has resulted in the mobilization of international funds for school feeding programs, the advancement of nutrition and school feeding projects, and the validation of diagnostics for sustainable production projects. The implications of the Centre's work are significant, as it has enabled the transfer of responsibilities from international organizations to national entities, promoting sustainable and multisectoral development. The Centre's partnerships with institutions such as the Brazilian Cooperation Agency and the Federal University of Lavras have also facilitated the dissemination of national school feeding programs and the creation of broader and more innovative solutions for the fight against hunger.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the WFP Centre of Excellence in Brazil's remote assistance and partnership efforts in supporting countries to combat hunger and malnutrition, particularly in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. The evaluation employed a qualitative methodology, gathering information from WFP Country Offices, government focal points in Brazil, and online media sources. Key findings indicate that the WFP Centre of Excellence in Brazil successfully implemented remote assistance and partnership efforts, including the development of a school feeding strategy for the Regional Bureau in Dakar, and the support of the "State of School Feeding Worldwide" publication. The Centre also collaborated with the Brazilian government, NGOs, and the private sector to promote sustainable food and nutrition security systems. Furthermore, the Centre supported the global SSTC team at the WFP Headquarters on actions that included a UNOSSC Webinar Event on global school feeding responses in times of COVID and the role of South-South Cooperation. The implications of these findings suggest that remote assistance and partnership efforts can be effective in supporting countries to combat hunger and malnutrition, particularly in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the WFP Centre of Excellence's technical assistance and advisory services in supporting countries to design and implement effective hunger solutions. The evaluation methodology involved a comprehensive review of the Centre's work, including its capacity strengthening activities, programme design, and transition strategies. Key findings indicate that the Centre's work has been instrumental in supporting countries to develop integrated, country-specific, and nationally-owned intervention strategies that bridge the gap between humanitarian and development responses. The Centre's capacity strengthening activities have been prioritized in all countries where WFP is acting as a channel for donor funding, with the objective of transitioning management and implementation of programmes to national entities once capacity is strong. The evaluation also highlights the Centre's role in promoting South-South cooperation and its recognition as a global reference in WFP Country Capacity Strengthening and South-South Cooperation. The findings have implications for the Centre's future work, emphasizing the need to continue supporting countries in developing effective hunger solutions and strengthening their capacity to manage and implement programmes sustainably.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) regional operations in Eastern Africa during 2021. The evaluation methodology involved an analysis of WFP's achievements, challenges, and partnerships in the region. Key findings include the provision of nutrition support to approximately 3.5 million people in northern Ethiopia, the establishment of a Regional Food Systems working group, and the implementation of inclusive community consultations to identify priority needs of women, men, and youth in targeted communities. Additionally, WFP supported the development of national school feeding policies and strategies in Ethiopia and Rwanda, and scaled up Homegrown School Feeding (HGSF) portfolios in Rwanda and Burundi. The evaluation also highlighted the importance of partnerships, with WFP sustaining regional partnership efforts to position itself as a partner of choice in nutrition and HIV/TB programming in the region. Implications of these findings suggest that WFP's regional operations in Eastern Africa were effective in addressing humanitarian needs, but that continued investment in capacity strengthening, resilience, and partnerships is necessary to further the Nutrition, HIV, and TB agenda in line with regional and global strategies.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of WFP's Engineering Services Division in supporting humanitarian and development efforts worldwide. The evaluation methodology involved a comprehensive review of WFP's Engineering portfolio, including case studies and project examples, to identify key areas of work and contributions to achieving a better future. The key findings of this evaluation indicate that WFP's Engineering Services Division has made significant contributions to protecting, restoring, creating, and enhancing basic infrastructure in food-insecure communities, with over 1 million beneficiaries positively impacted through infrastructure projects and services. The division's expertise in project management, infrastructure development, and maintenance has been instrumental in supporting WFP's humanitarian assistance in various regions, including Somalia, South Sudan, and Cox's Bazar. The evaluation also highlights the division's commitment to creating a sustainable future, with environmentally friendly initiatives and a focus on addressing global challenges. The implications of this evaluation suggest that WFP's Engineering Services Division plays a critical role in supporting the organization's humanitarian objectives and ensuring a better future for the people it serves.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme (WFP) Ethics Office in promoting a culture of ethics and accountability within the organization. The evaluation methodology involved an examination of the Ethics Office's activities and achievements over the period from 1 January to 31 December 2024, as outlined in the annual report submitted to the Executive Board. Key findings indicate that the Ethics Office has been successful in fostering a culture of ethics and accountability, with over 20 percent of employees seeking advice from the office at least twice in 2024, demonstrating continued trust in the office. The office has also been promoting understanding of the policy on preventing and responding to sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) through outreach and awareness activities. Furthermore, the Ethics Office has been providing advocacy and guidance on the incorporation of ethical standards into WFP policies, practices, and standards, and has been supporting the organization in fostering an ethical culture of integrity and transparency. The evaluation highlights the importance of the Ethics Office's work in risk prevention, upholding WFP's values and code of conduct, and ensuring the organization's trustworthiness and capability to deliver on its life-saving and life-changing mandate.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) specialized unit, the Fast IT and Telecommunications Emergency and Support Team (FITTEST), in providing critical information and communication technology (ICT) capabilities during sudden-onset emergencies. Utilizing a qualitative methodology, the evaluation examined FITTEST's 25 years of experience in delivering expert end-to-end support in complex, multi-stakeholder, multi-hazard, and multicultural environments. Key findings indicate that FITTEST successfully deploys ICT capabilities, conducts hands-on technical missions, and provides surge support for field operations, thereby enabling humanitarian operations to stay connected and respond effectively. The evaluation's implications suggest that FITTEST's expertise and emergency stock can be leveraged to enhance the WFP's response to emergencies, ultimately improving the resilience and preparedness of affected communities.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of FITTEST operations in ensuring emergency preparedness and sustainable humanitarian response. The evaluation methodology involved examining the critical elements of FITTEST operations, including project and equipment management, emergency preparedness, and connectivity and equipment provision. Key findings highlighted the importance of preparedness in mitigating risks and ensuring resilience in the face of disasters, as exemplified by the devastating impact of flooding on an internally displaced persons camp. The evaluation also underscored the crucial role of technology in managing humanitarian operations, including the provision of data and voice connectivity and equipment sourcing, management, and maintenance. The implications of these findings suggest that FITTEST operations must prioritize emergency preparedness, steady-state preparedness, and technology-enabled management to ensure sustainable and resilient humanitarian response.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of FITTEST specialists in providing security communications solutions and supporting humanitarian operations in emergency response readiness. The evaluation employed a qualitative methodology, involving analysis of FITTEST's activities, including risk assessments, needs assessments, coordination, and planning of response efforts. Key findings indicate that FITTEST specialists have successfully identified and implemented appropriate security communications solutions, supported customers on technology infrastructure and emergency response readiness, and strengthened existing coordination mechanisms in response to disruptions caused by conflicts and natural disasters. The evaluation also highlights FITTEST's ability to create customized packages tailored to specific customer needs, and its transparent pricing model. The implications of these findings suggest that FITTEST specialists can play a critical role in supporting the humanitarian community in emergency response situations, and that their services can be effectively integrated into humanitarian operations to enhance response effectiveness.

This evaluation aimed to assess the implementation of the World Food Programme's (WFP) Global Artificial Intelligence (AI) Strategy, which seeks to scale the adoption of AI across the organization to transform business functions and modernize operations. The evaluation objective was to identify key areas for strengthening, including the proactive pursuit of impactful AI solutions, AI governance, and the development of an AI culture. The methodology involved a gap analysis and maturity level assessment, which revealed the need for a world-class AI technology infrastructure, a holistic approach to AI governance, and the building of an AI culture anchored in learning and knowledge management. Key findings included the importance of leveraging existing processes, people, and technology artefacts, as well as the need for collaboration and effective use of expertise and knowledge across WFP divisions, country offices, and regional bureaux. The implications of this evaluation are that WFP must prioritize the development of AI-specific policies, guidelines, and standards, and establish a comprehensive AI Governance Framework to ensure the responsible and ethical development and deployment of AI within the organization. By fostering a deep understanding of AI and cultivating an AI-centric culture, WFP can ensure that its workforce is prepared to leverage AI effectively, driving innovation and enhancing operational efficiency.

This evaluation aims to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) Global Data Strategy 2024-2026 in establishing a modern data estate and promoting data-driven decision-making. The evaluation methodology involves analyzing the strategy's four strategic pillars: Delivering with intent and evidence, Architecting best of class data services, Effective and efficient data foundations, and Responsibly empowering people. Key findings indicate that the strategy aims to strengthen data architecture, management, and governance capabilities, and to develop a data-driven workforce and culture. The evaluation also highlights the importance of data quality, interoperability, and security in achieving the strategy's objectives. The implications of the evaluation suggest that successful implementation of the strategy will enable WFP to make informed decisions, improve outcomes, and maximize the value of its data and analytics.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of environmental and social risk management measures in a project implemented by UNICEF and WFP in collaboration with various stakeholders. The evaluation objective was to ensure that the project's interventions met the objectives and requirements of the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and adhered to UNICEF's and WFP's Environmental and Social Standards.

The methodology involved the preparation of an Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF) and supporting Environmental and Social (E&S) management instruments, including Project Labor Management Procedures (LMP). The ESMF guided UNICEF and WFP in assessing environmental and social risks and impacts, identifying necessary mitigation measures, and monitoring the implementation of E&S measures.
