The project implementation involved direct workers, contracted workers, and community workers, with requirements extended to subcontractors.

Key findings included the effective incorporation of E&S instruments into procurement and contract documents, monitoring through reporting mechanisms, and compliance with environmental and social risks and impacts associated with the project. The project also implemented various measures to manage environmental and social risks, including capacity building plans for service providers and contractors, awareness raising and training for stakeholders, and grievance redress mechanisms.

The implications of this evaluation are that UNICEF and WFP have demonstrated a commitment to environmental and social risk management in the project, with a focus on ensuring the safety and well-being of project workers, beneficiaries, and communities. The effective implementation of E&S measures has contributed to the project's overall success and has set a precedent for future projects.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the IASC Championship on Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (PSEAH) in strengthening WFP's commitment to a humanitarian system free from sexual exploitation and abuse. The evaluation methodology involved monitoring key initiatives and engagements of the Executive Director, including meetings with UN leadership, the UN High-Level Steering Group on PSEA, and the IASC PSEAH Global Workshop. Key findings indicate that the Executive Director has amplified the voices of high-risk communities, increased awareness of the need for collective action, and strengthened WFP's commitment to a victim-centered approach. The evaluation also highlights the establishment of a global advisory group consisting of women-led NGOs and civil society, the promotion of interagency standards on PSEAH, and the development of guidelines and resources to reduce SEA risks in humanitarian assistance. The implications of these findings suggest that the IASC Championship has been successful in driving collective commitment and support for PSEAH across the organization, and that continued efforts are needed to strengthen cooperation and ensure a collective accountability and leadership across the sector.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the UN World Food Programme's (WFP) revised food distribution procedures in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The evaluation methodology involved an examination of the revised procedures, which included alternative arrangements for individuals unable to attend distributions, and adherence to public health guidelines, such as the World Health Organization's (WHO) COVID-19 protection measures. Key findings indicate that the WFP has implemented measures to mitigate the risk of COVID-19 transmission during food distributions, including staff awareness of public health guidelines, offloading and organizing rations, and regular hand sanitation and hygiene practices. The implications of these findings suggest that the WFP's revised procedures have contributed to a safer and more efficient food distribution process, ultimately supporting the delivery of essential food assistance to vulnerable populations.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of World Food Programme (WFP) initiatives in addressing the needs and capacities of Indigenous Peoples. To achieve this objective, the evaluation employed a comprehensive methodology that involved analyzing existing programming and documentation across WFP's portfolio. Key findings indicate that Indigenous Peoples are disproportionately vulnerable to structural inequality, discrimination, displacement, conflict, and violence, necessitating culturally sensitive and context-specific programming. The evaluation highlights the critical role that Indigenous Peoples' knowledge and practices can play in environmental management, early warning, and food production. The WFP's efforts to harness these capacities are aligned with the UN Call to Action: Building an Inclusive, Sustainable and Resilient Future with Indigenous Peoples (endorsed by the Chief Executives Board in 2020), underscoring the importance of integrating Indigenous Peoples' perspectives and expertise into WFP's programming.

This evaluation aimed to assess the World Food Programme's (WFP) Information and Technology (I&T) Strategy 2023-2026, with the objective of driving the I&T environment and governance to enable the organization to prioritize and deliver value-added work. The evaluation methodology involved extensive consultations with business stakeholders across WFP in 2022 and a Strategic Evaluation on WFP's Use of Technology in Constrained Environments. Key findings indicate that the I&T Strategy makes the case for how digital technology and data can reinforce WFP's strength and reach, propelling the organization towards achieving its Strategic Outcomes for 2022-2025. The evaluation highlights the importance of a Digital Blueprint, which will bring together the I&T elements of WFP to amplify the value of I&T to the organization. The report also emphasizes the need for robust capacity building for staff in all facets of emergency preparedness and response, including I&T and data analytics skills. Furthermore, the evaluation stresses the importance of gathering data that helps WFP better understand and target the people it serves, and the need for a customer-driven I&T culture of support to business units and operations. The evaluation concludes that the WFP I&T Strategy 2023-2026 has the potential to bring a cascade of sustainable benefits to communities by establishing clear operating procedures, conditions, and capabilities for engaging with governments on I&T projects.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) response to the food security crisis in Lebanon. The study employed an Integrated Phase Classification (IPC) food security analysis and qualitative assessments to evaluate the impact of WFP's assistance on the population. Key findings indicate that approximately 2 million people (37% of the total population) experienced acute food insecurity between September and December 2022. While cash assistance increased purchasing power, it was insufficient to offset price increases and currency depreciation. Notably, the school feeding programme showed encouraging results in improving children's nutrition. The evaluation also highlighted the importance of ensuring safe and dignified access to assistance, with all beneficiaries, including 82,000 persons with disabilities, reporting positive experiences. The findings inform WFP's Country Strategic Plan 2023-2025, which aims to sustain crisis response, support safety nets, and enhance food systems, ultimately contributing to improved food security outcomes for the Lebanese population.

This humanitarian evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of assistance provided to conflict-affected populations in South Lebanon. The evaluation employed a mixed-methods approach, combining data from various sources, including internally displaced persons (IDPs) returns, food insecurity projections, and assistance coverage rates. Key findings indicate that, despite some stabilization following the displacement crisis, food insecurity is projected to rise, affecting 1.24 million people (23 percent of the population) by October 2025. Additionally, severe funding shortfalls and delays led to a 37 percent reduction in assistance provided by the World Food Programme (WFP), reaching 876,000 people in June, down from 1.4 million in January. However, new contributions and a retargeting exercise allowed WFP to scale up assistance to 76 percent of the Needs-Based Plan, covering 663,000 refugees. The evaluation also highlights the importance of coordination and capacity building, as evidenced by the training of 500 Ministry of Social Affairs (MoSA) staff and the initiation of home visits by WFP-trained social workers to assess the needs of conflict-affected Lebanese families.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) efforts to promote disability inclusion in its activities in Lebanon. The evaluation methodology involved an examination of WFP's implementation of its Disability Inclusion Action Plan, which is aligned with the WFP Lebanon Country Strategic Plan (2023-2025). Key findings indicate that WFP has taken significant steps to ensure the inclusion of persons with disabilities, including enhanced targeting approaches, regular assessments of redemption and distribution sites, and support for out-of-school children with disabilities through the Dirasa Programme. Additionally, WFP has strengthened its capacity to support individuals with disabilities through training of Disability Inclusion champions and adapted its assistance to meet the needs of individuals such as Laila, a 56-year-old woman with a physical disability. The evaluation also highlights WFP's efforts to create a more inclusive workplace, including refined recruitment practices and sensitization sessions for security personnel. Implications of these findings suggest that WFP's commitment to disability inclusion has the potential to improve the lives of individuals with disabilities in Lebanon, and that continued prioritization of this area will be essential in achieving the goals outlined in the WFP Lebanon Country Strategic Plan.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of fuel delivery to Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) facilities by the World Food Programme (WFP) amidst operational challenges. The methodology involved analyzing the impact of external factors on fuel delivery, including data availability, security incidents, and harsh weather conditions. Key findings revealed that the initial fuel delivery target of 6 million litres at 57 cents/litre was hindered by oversupply of fuel from alternative sources, security incidents, and weather conditions, necessitating a revision of the distribution target to 64 cents/litre. The evaluation's findings underscore the importance of considering external factors and adapting to changing circumstances in humanitarian operations to ensure the continuity of essential services.

This evaluation aimed to assess the accessibility of assistance provided by the World Food Programme (WFP) to unique beneficiaries, with a focus on identifying challenges and necessary adjustments to ensure safe and dignified access to assistance. The evaluation methodology involved consolidating data from various sources, including household interviews, process monitoring, transaction data, and feedback from the call centre. Key findings indicate that travel time to redemption points (ATM or MTO) and waiting time to redeem assistance have decreased over time, with average travel times ranging from 15 to 30 minutes and waiting times ranging from 0 to 60 minutes. Additionally, the cost to reach distribution sites has fluctuated, with an average cost of 250,000-350,000 LBP. The evaluation also found that satisfaction with the quality and quantity of food parcels has remained relatively stable, with an average satisfaction rate of 8.5-9.0. These findings have implications for the WFP's efforts to ensure that assistance is accessible, efficient, and effective in meeting the needs of beneficiaries.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) assistance modalities in addressing the evolving needs and challenges of Syrian refugees and vulnerable Lebanese populations in Lebanon. The evaluation employed a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative data on food security and economic vulnerability indicators with qualitative insights from community-based participatory planning (CBPP) consultations. Key findings indicate that WFP's support has been critical in mitigating the impact of the economic crisis and COVID-19 pandemic on food security, with 81 percent of assisted Syrian refugee households unable to afford the Survival Minimum Expenditure Basket (SMEB) without WFP's cash support. The evaluation also highlights the importance of targeting assistance to the most vulnerable populations, with WFP's household targeting approach using food security and economic vulnerability indicators to ensure that those most in need are reached. The findings suggest that WFP's support has contributed to improved food security and well-being among the target populations, with 42,000 displaced Lebanese in South Lebanon assisted with food support and 62,000 newly arrived Syrians reached with emergency food assistance. The evaluation's implications suggest that WFP's continued support is essential to address the alarming projected levels of acute food insecurity in Lebanon, with 1.24 million people expected to face acute food insecurity by October 2025.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) logistics operation in response to the Beirut port explosion and the ongoing economic crisis in Lebanon. The methodology involved analyzing the procurement and distribution of food parcels, including the sourcing of wheat flour and other essential commodities. Key findings indicate that the WFP's in-kind food operation has been critical in supporting vulnerable Lebanese, with 80% of food procured internationally and 20% sourced locally to ensure timeliness and benefit the local economy. The operation has also enabled the secure storage of COVID-19 vaccines and facilitated the delivery of fuel to facilities in need. The evaluation highlights the importance of maintaining the in-kind food operation and supply chain arrangements to support food security in Lebanon, as well as the need for harmonized customs clearances for UN agencies to ensure efficient and cost-effective services. The implications of these findings suggest that continued support for the WFP's logistics operation is essential to addressing the ongoing economic crisis and ensuring the well-being of vulnerable populations in Lebanon.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) nutrition and HIV programming in achieving its corporate nutrition results and contributing to global nutrition targets and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The evaluation methodology involved consolidating data from the Annual Performance Report, Annual Country Reports, and indicators tracked in the Corporate Results Framework. Key findings included the reach of 64 million people through nutrition-sensitive programmes, the embedding of nutrition in social protection systems in 41 countries, and the scaling up of digital innovations to strengthen programme delivery and monitoring. The evaluation also highlighted WFP's commitments to improving access to and consumption of nutritious diets, reducing malnutrition in humanitarian settings, and expanding its engagement with national counterparts to strengthen evidence-based decision-making. The evaluation demonstrated that WFP's integrated prevention package, which includes nutritionally adequate household food assistance, social and behaviour change programming, and linkages to health and nutrition services, had measurable impact in reducing malnutrition. The evaluation also noted that WFP continued to prioritize the quality and coverage of its interventions despite challenges such as funding constraints, access limitations, and supply chain disruptions. The evaluation concluded that WFP's efforts had contributed to measurable improvements in knowledge and skills among national staff, and that the organization remained committed to delivering high-impact nutrition responses that are equitable, sustainable, and scalable.

This evaluation aimed to assess the food security situation in Tonga, with a focus on household food consumption patterns, coping strategies, and income sources. The study employed a mobile Vulnerability Analysis and Mapping (mVAM) survey, utilizing telephone interviews conducted across five administrative divisions in Tonga between October and November 2024. A sample of 1,208 households was randomly selected using random-digit dialing. The key findings indicate that, as of October 2024, 91 percent of Tongan households reported adequate food intake, a slight decline from September 2023. However, 7 percent of households had borderline consumption, and 2 percent experienced poor consumption levels. Notably, insufficient intake of nutrient-rich foods, such as iron, protein, and Vitamin A, was reported by 39 percent, 14 percent, and 25 percent of households, respectively. The use of stress coping strategies, such as borrowing money or depleting savings, decreased from above 30 percent in mid-2022 to 19 percent in October 2024. The evaluation also highlights regional disparities, with Niua and Tongatapu reporting higher proportions of households with insufficient iron intake. The findings suggest that, while food consumption patterns are generally at acceptable levels, there are concerns regarding income sources, with salary/wages being the primary source of income for 60 percent of respondents. The implications of these findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to address regional disparities and ensure access to nutrient-rich foods, particularly in areas with high proportions of households experiencing poor food security.

This evaluation aimed to assess the impact of the global food crisis on Fiji's economy and household food security in 2023. The study employed a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative data from the Reserve Bank of Fiji and qualitative insights from World Food Programme (WFP) remote surveys. Key findings indicate that the Fijian Dollar's depreciation against major currencies, particularly the US Dollar, significantly contributed to the rise in food prices, with essential food items experiencing the greatest price increases. The exchange rate fluctuations and remittance inflows played a crucial role in mitigating the economic challenges faced by Fiji, with remittances accounting for 9.7 percent of the total GDP in December 2023. However, the study also highlights the vulnerability of rural households to food price volatility, with 62.2 percent of the poor population residing in rural areas. The evaluation suggests that Fiji's economy demonstrated a degree of robustness in the face of global economic shocks, with remittances supporting household food security and mitigating the impact of labour immobility and disruptions in key sectors.

The evaluation objective of the World Food Programme's (WFP) people policy is to establish a coherent framework for excellence in people management by outlining the organization's workforce vision, priorities, and commitments, and its expectations for employees' behavior towards each other and towards the organization. The methodology employed involves a systematic and strategic approach to workforce planning, management, and operationalization, with a focus on fostering a spirit of inclusiveness, respect, teamwork, openness, and transparency. The key findings of this evaluation include the importance of a proactive approach to people management, the need for a workforce able to play capacity building, capacity strengthening, and technical advisory roles, and the importance of addressing the need to cultivate a healthy and respectful workplace culture. The implications of this evaluation are that WFP must adopt a more systematic and strategic approach to workforce planning, management, and operationalization, and prioritize the development of a diverse, committed, skilled, and high-performing workforce that is selected on merit and operates in a healthy and inclusive work environment. This will enable WFP to deliver on its mission and achieve its vision of a future workforce that is capable of saving and changing the lives of the people it serves.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) response to Typhoon Odette in the Philippines. The evaluation methodology involved an examination of WFP's emergency response activities, including food assistance distributions, cash and voucher assistance, and logistics support. Key findings indicate that WFP was among the first to respond to the disaster, providing critical support to affected populations through its partners, including CARE, Catholic Relief Services (CRS), and Action Against Hunger (AAH). The evaluation highlights WFP's ability to adapt its response to the evolving needs of the affected communities, prioritizing cash and voucher assistance in areas where markets were functional. The use of WFP's beneficiary and transfer management platform, SCOPE, ensured efficient registration and management of beneficiaries. The evaluation also notes the importance of community feedback mechanisms, which were utilized to inform program management and decision-making. The findings suggest that WFP's emergency response was effective in meeting essential needs targets, with beneficiaries reporting satisfaction with the assistance targeting process and the distribution process. The evaluation implies that WFP's emergency response was well-coordinated with the Government of the Philippines, with WFP providing critical logistics support, including transportation and storage capacity. The evaluation concludes that WFP's emergency response to Typhoon Odette was effective in providing critical support to affected populations, and that the organization's commitment to building the logistics capacity of local government units and implementing partners has contributed to improved disaster preparedness and response.

This regional evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of local and regional food procurement pilots in Uganda, Ethiopia, and Sudan. The evaluation employed a mixed-methods approach to examine the integration of procurement and programming interventions in addressing bottlenecks in value chains and promoting local food systems, livelihoods, and resilience of smallholder farmers. Key findings indicate that integrated efforts, particularly direct procurements, improved smallholder farmers' capacity, yields, and crop quality, resulting in increased incomes (5-15% above market value). However, challenges in traceability, definitional clarity on smallholder farmers, and contextualization of conditionality thresholds hindered success in indirect procurement modalities through traders. The evaluation highlights the importance of incentivizing pro-smallholder farmer purchases and suggests that addressing these challenges is crucial for scaling up local procurement initiatives.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of WFP's humanitarian response services in fragile contexts where commercial aviation options were limited due to conflict or climatic disasters. The evaluation methodology involved analyzing the impact of these services on the timely delivery of humanitarian assistance to vulnerable populations. Key findings revealed that WFP's services enabled partners to reach vulnerable individuals with critical support, thereby mitigating the effects of limited access in fragile contexts. The implications of these findings highlight the importance of WFP's humanitarian response services in ensuring the delivery of timely assistance to those in need, particularly in situations where commercial options are unavailable.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) food safety and quality (FSQ) initiatives in 2023. The methodology involved monitoring and analysis of FSQ-related activities, including food supplier audits, assessments, and training workshops. Key findings indicate a 50 percent decrease in total food impacted from 2022 to 2023, with 72,985 metric tons of food affected in 2023. The FSQ Terrain (FOSTER) platform was utilized by 70 percent of the region, falling short of the target of 95 percent due to changes in Sudan and vendor exclusion. The evaluation also highlights successful partnerships, such as the agreement with the Rwanda Standards Board, and capacity-building initiatives, including training workshops and onboarding of local wheat millers. The implications of these findings suggest that WFP's commitment to providing safe, nutritious, and high-quality food to those in need is being implemented, but there is room for improvement in FSQ management and logistics capabilities, particularly in Somalia.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) logistics operations in responding to crises in the East Africa and Horn of Africa region. The evaluation methodology involved an examination of WFP's logistics network, including ports, routes, and warehouses, as well as the use of the Global Commodity Management Facility (GCMF) to purchase food at favourable prices. Key findings include the successful dispatch of over 2.9 million MT of food to various operations, providing assistance to nearly 40 million people, and the use of cash assistance in markets where feasible, empowering beneficiaries with flexibility and autonomy. Despite challenges such as increased country transport costs and limited access to fuel and cash, WFP's Logistics team maintained a high data reliability index score and implemented tracking measures to ensure the integrity of food distribution. The evaluation also highlights the establishment of new food supply corridors, the scaling up of cash assistance, and the launch of digital systems to boost operational efficiency and effectiveness. The implications of these findings are that WFP's logistics operations have been effective in responding to crises in the region, and that the use of digital systems and cash assistance has contributed to improved operational efficiency and effectiveness.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) response to the COVID-19 pandemic in Uganda. The evaluation methodology involved a review of WFP's supply chain and engineering efforts, as well as its collaboration with the government and humanitarian actors. Key findings indicate that WFP's efforts, supported by UKAID and USAID, resulted in the establishment of semi-permanent structures, incinerators, and district stores to support health care waste management and regional stockpiling of infectious disease emergency commodities. Additionally, WFP provided transportation services to enable the distribution of government commodities across the country. The evaluation highlights the successful implementation of the Presidential Urban Food Assistance programme, which included the construction of isolation facilities and the establishment of warehouses dedicated to Ministry of Health commodities. The implications of these findings suggest that WFP's response to the pandemic was effective in supporting the government and humanitarian actors in containing the spread of COVID-19 in Uganda.

This evaluation aimed to assess the impact of the 2022 La Niña phenomenon on rainfall and rice production in Indonesia. The study employed a comparative analysis of rainfall accumulation and long-term averages, as well as field monitoring reports from the Ministry of Agriculture, to evaluate the effects of extreme rainfall events on rice cultivation. Key findings indicate that La Niña caused higher-than-normal rainfall across Indonesia, resulting in localized extreme rains that led to floods, landslides, and crop failures in several districts. The total area of paddy crop failures between December 2021 and February 2022 reached 19,000 hectares, with 96% attributed to floods. Notably, despite the ongoing La Niña situation, overall rice production in Indonesia significantly increased compared to the same period in 2021, likely due to extreme rainfall events. The evaluation's implications suggest that the Indonesian government and agricultural stakeholders should continue to monitor and prepare for the potential impacts of La Niña on rice production and food security.

This evaluation aimed to assess the potential impact of climate change on food security and nutrition in Indonesia. The evaluation employed a desk review of existing data and reports from the Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) and other relevant sources. Key findings indicate that 63% of areas in Indonesia have started to experience the dry season, with all areas within Java, Bali, and Nusa Tenggara, as well as some provinces in Sumatera, Kalimantan, and Sulawesi, predicted to be impacted. The evaluation also found that 12 provinces were categorized as under watch for possible degradation of food and nutrition security, with 26 of 34 provinces experiencing food availability under watch. Furthermore, the onset of El Niño is likely to occur in the second half of 2023, potentially negatively impacting rice production. The evaluation highlights the need for early warning systems and climate-resilient agriculture practices to mitigate the impacts of climate change on food security and nutrition in Indonesia.

This evaluation aimed to assess the rainfall patterns and drought conditions in Indonesia during the first quarter of 2023 and forecast the potential impacts of El Niño on the country's climate. The evaluation employed a qualitative and quantitative analysis of rainfall data from various sources, including the Climate Hazards Group Infrared Precipitation (CHIRPS) dataset and the World Food Programme's (WFP) Seasonal Explorer. The key findings indicate that, compared to the 30-year average (1991-2020), rainfall patterns in Indonesia during the first quarter of 2023 were mostly within the normal range, except for the third week of January and March. However, above-average rainfall was observed in several regions, including Sumatera, Kalimantan, and Maluku, which may have positive impacts on agricultural activities. Conversely, below-average rainfall was observed in regions such as Bali, Nusa Tenggara Timur, and Nusa Tenggara Barat, leading to drought conditions and negatively affecting vegetation growth. The evaluation also forecasts that El Niño will bring drier and warmer conditions to Indonesia, with a 90% probability of occurrence during March-May 2023. The predicted impacts of El Niño include low to moderate rainfall between May and July 2023, with below-normal rainfall expected in several regions, including Jawa, Bali, Nusa Tenggara, and southern Sumatera. The evaluation's findings and forecasts have significant implications for agricultural activities, water availability, and food security in Indonesia, highlighting the need for proactive measures to mitigate the potential impacts of El Niño.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) approach to building resilience in vulnerable populations. To achieve this objective, the evaluation employed a mixed-methods approach, combining desk reviews, stakeholder consultations, and field assessments. Key findings indicate that WFP's integrated resilience building approach, which leverages its comparative strengths in emergency response, human capital development, and social safety nets, has shown promising results in reducing reliance on unconditional humanitarian assistance and promoting lasting impact. The evaluation highlights the importance of WFP's commitment to mainstreaming gender equality, women's empowerment, protection, and accountability to affected populations in its programming. Furthermore, the evaluation notes that WFP's capacity to respond to large-scale crises and its ability to work with key partners to anticipate and prepare for crises are critical to its success. The evaluation also emphasizes the need for WFP to continue investing in complementing and strengthening nationally-led systems in emergency preparedness and response, social protection, and food systems to mitigate the human and financial costs of crises. Overall, the evaluation suggests that WFP's approach to resilience building has the potential to contribute to food security and peace, but requires continued flexibility, pragmatism, and progressive adaptation to contextual changes and the needs on the ground.

The evaluation objective of the United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS) in Haiti is to ensure continuous humanitarian access and effective emergency response in the face of a protracted political, security, and socio-economic crisis. To achieve this objective, UNHAS will maintain its current operational fleet, comprising one fixed-wing aircraft and one helicopter, to provide uninterrupted access for aid organizations. The methodology involves the continued operation of daily flights to Petion-Ville and nine additional destinations throughout Haiti, facilitating the rapid deployment of aid workers, the transport of critical life-saving supplies, and the execution of emergency medical evacuations. Key findings indicate that 5.4 million people in Haiti are facing acute food insecurity, with 2 million experiencing emergency levels of hunger. The suspension of commercial flights and the escalation of violence have severely limited the movement of humanitarian aid and personnel, highlighting the critical need for UNHAS services. The implications of this evaluation are that UNHAS will continue to operate with a standard UNHAS governance structure, with the Steering Committee revisiting the framework if funding challenges persist. The estimated cost to continue operating UNHAS Haiti for 3 months is US$3.9 million, and operations will be scaled down or discontinued when reliable commercial aviation services are available or overland access improves.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the joint cash programming between the World Food Programme (WFP) and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in providing monthly cash assistance to vulnerable Syrian refugees in Lebanon for food and other essential needs. The evaluation employed a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative data from the WFP and UNHCR's joint cash programming with qualitative insights from frontline staff, community structures, and surveyed assisted families. Key findings indicate that despite the continued high needs of refugee families, the joint cash programming has provided essential support, with 228,300 families assisted in 2023. However, funding shortfalls led to a 30 percent reduction in the number of assisted refugee households from December 2023 onwards, reaching only 176,700 households. The evaluation also highlights the importance of dual currency redemption, which improved the ability of assisted families to access a wider range of higher-quality food and reduced difficulties in redeeming assistance. The findings suggest that the joint cash programming has made a significant impact in reducing food insecurity and enhancing livelihoods among vulnerable Syrian refugees. However, inadequate funding continues to hamper the continuity of the programme, emphasizing the need to sustain assistance to vulnerable households and increase coverage and transfer values to meet recommended standards. The evaluation's implications underscore the importance of continued support to refugee families to prevent regression into higher food insecurity and socio-economic vulnerability levels.

This humanitarian evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of emergency response interventions in Ukraine, focusing on food assistance and mine action efforts. The evaluation methodology involved an examination of program implementation, including the distribution of food and cash assistance in high-risk areas, as well as collaboration with specialist demining organizations to support landmine clearance and agricultural recovery. Key findings indicate that a significant proportion of food distributed is sourced locally in Ukraine, and assistance is delivered in frontline regions, supporting local economic recovery. However, the evaluation also highlights challenges in accessing areas occupied by the Russian Federation, despite joint requests from WFP and other UN agencies. Furthermore, the evaluation notes the repeated targeting and damage of civilian infrastructure, including humanitarian assistance storage and distribution facilities, by strikes. These findings have significant implications for future humanitarian response efforts in Ukraine, emphasizing the need for sustained support to local economic recovery, continued collaboration with demining organizations, and enhanced protection of civilian infrastructure.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) support for Ukrainian grain and food exports under the Grain from Ukraine initiative. The evaluation methodology involved analyzing data on WFP's chartering of vessels and procurement of Ukrainian food commodities from July 2022 to the present. Key findings indicate that WFP's direct support for Ukrainian food exports has resulted in the transportation of over 289,552 metric tons of commodities to 18 critical WFP operations in various countries, ultimately feeding over 8 million people. This achievement demonstrates the initiative's potential to alleviate food insecurity in vulnerable regions. The implications of this evaluation highlight the importance of continued international support for WFP's efforts to facilitate Ukrainian food exports and ensure a stable global food supply.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the United Nations World Food Programme's (WFP) technical support to national social protection systems. The evaluation methodology involved analyzing data from 20 countries where WFP provided technical advice and guidance on social protection, resulting in increased coverage for over 834 million people through national social protection systems programmes indirectly supported by WFP. Key findings indicate that WFP's comparative advantage in social protection lies in its ability to leverage its deep field presence, practical operational expertise, and understanding of poverty and vulnerability to help governments develop solutions that enable households to meet their food security, nutrition, and other essential needs. WFP's work in social protection is strengthened through partnerships and collaborations with donors, other agencies, and academic partners, as well as rich exchanges of knowledge and evidence with the global social protection community. The evaluation also highlights WFP's key role in working on social protection in fragile and conflict settings, engaging in 80% of the countries on the World Bank's FCV 2023 list of countries affected by fragility, conflict, and violence. Implications of these findings suggest that WFP's support for coordination efforts and the institutionalisation of coordination platforms is crucial for improving national social protection systems' responsiveness to shocks, and that WFP's partnerships and collaborations are essential for achieving its objectives in social protection.

This evaluation aims to assess the World Food Programme's (WFP) response to escalating humanitarian needs in 2025. The evaluation objective is to understand the impact of funding shortfalls on WFP's assistance and capacity to address severe needs. The methodology involves analyzing WFP's global presence, school-meal programmes, and capacity-building initiatives. Key findings indicate that WFP is facing significant challenges in maintaining assistance levels due to restricted humanitarian access and funding shortfalls. Furthermore, the organization is scaling back assistance and refocusing on the most severe needs. The implications of these findings suggest that WFP's ability to achieve its zero-hunger goal by 2030 may be compromised, highlighting the need for increased funding and support to sustain national policies and programmes.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) response to acute food insecurity in Asia and the Pacific in 2024. The evaluation employed a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative data on the number of people reached by WFP's food assistance programs with qualitative insights from beneficiaries and partners. Key findings indicate that 88 million people in the region faced acute food insecurity in 2024, a significant increase from 28 million in 2019. WFP's emergency response in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and other countries reached over 16 million people, with 62% receiving food assistance, 31% receiving cash, and 7% receiving food vouchers. However, the global funding crisis limited the scope of WFP's response, with only 12% of needs addressed in the summer season and 41% during the scaled-up winter response. The evaluation highlights the need for anticipatory action and preparedness in emergencies, with WFP's anticipatory action programme in Bangladesh supporting over 628,000 people ahead of Cyclone Remal and the Jamuna Basin floods. The evaluation also underscores the importance of strengthening national infrastructure and supporting community development projects to reduce disaster risks. Implications of the evaluation suggest that the humanitarian community's ability to respond to emerging needs is limited, and that a targeted alignment of resources is necessary to ensure an integrated approach to addressing the intersectionality of needs. The evaluation recommends continued advocacy for investments in preparedness and preventive measures, as well as a commitment to strengthening innovation, partnerships, and integrated programmatic approaches to maximize the efficiency and impact of interventions.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) Environmental Plan of Action 2030 (EPACT) in reducing the organization's environmental impacts. The evaluation methodology involved tracking greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, water usage, and pollution, as well as monitoring the implementation of the EPACT's targets and milestones. Key findings include the successful reduction of greenhouse gas emissions by 35% since 2010, the development of a basic methodology to estimate environmental impact, and the mainstreaming of environmental sustainability considerations in WFP's operations. Implications of these findings include the potential for WFP to reduce its relative emissions by 45% by 2030, the need to establish a baseline and methodology for scope 3 emissions, and the importance of enhancing the monitoring of environmental sustainability to achieve the goals outlined in the EPACT.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) Regional Urban Preparedness Initiative in reducing food insecurity and malnutrition in urban communities across Southern Africa, particularly in Lesotho, Madagascar, Mozambique, and Zimbabwe. The evaluation methodology involved a review of project activities and outcomes from Phases I and II, which were implemented from 2021 to 2026, with a focus on the project's strategic partnerships, capacity building, and policy influence. Key findings indicate that the project has strengthened Country Offices and government capacities in urban programming, shaped national urban response mechanisms, and embedded urban resilience strategies within national policies. The project's methodologies and evidence-driven approach have contributed to a shift from research to policy to action in urban disaster preparedness across Southern Africa. The evaluation's implications suggest that actionable frameworks, capacity building, and partnerships are essential for addressing the worsening climate and food security crisis in the region, particularly in urban areas.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of partnerships between the World Food Programme (WFP) and national meteorological agencies in strengthening their capacities for Anticipatory Action (AA) in response to climate-related hazards. The methodology involved fostering partnerships with the Djibouti National Meteorological Agency (DNMA) and the Ethiopian Meteorological Institute (EMI) to equip them with necessary forecasting skills and tools. Key findings include the successful development of drought forecasting tools, such as the Maproom, and the implementation of drought anticipatory action activations in Ethiopia's Somali Region. The partnerships also facilitated the exchange of climate data and forecast information among regional countries, enhancing the capacity of meteorological agencies to generate seasonal and sub-seasonal forecasts. The implications of this evaluation are that the partnerships have contributed to building a network of experts who can support AA in the region, fostering an environment for sharing best practices and addressing common challenges.

This evaluation aims to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) Strategy to improve diets and address malnutrition (2024-2030) in achieving its mission to provide immediate assistance in emergencies and address the root causes of hunger. The evaluation methodology involves an analysis of WFP's programmes, processes, and partnerships to identify key areas of focus and opportunities for integration of nutrition activities and objectives across global operations. Key findings include the importance of leveraging WFP's comparative advantage as the largest provider of food and nutrition assistance worldwide, and the need to optimise opportunities to integrate nutrition activities and objectives across its global operations. The evaluation also highlights the importance of using data, evidence, and analytics to make effective use of resources, and working in partnership to support sustainable solutions. The implications of this evaluation are that WFP should prioritise its efforts to address malnutrition, foster efficiency, and optimise impact, and leverage its work on social protection, school meals, climate adaptation, and resilient food systems to promote the local production, transformation, distribution, and consumption of diverse, nutrient-dense foods.

The evaluation objective of WFP's climate change policy is to assess the effectiveness of its climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction efforts in supporting food-insecure communities and promoting sustainable development. The methodology employed involves an analysis of WFP's climate change policy and its implementation, including its alignment with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the Paris Agreement. Key findings include the successful implementation of climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction programs, such as the Sahel Integrated Resilience program, which has improved the adaptive capacity of 4 million people in five countries. Additionally, WFP has demonstrated its ability to connect food-insecure communities to climate risk insurance solutions, leverage sovereign climate risk insurance for humanitarian operations, and use machine learning for hazard early warning applications. The implications of these findings are that WFP's climate change policy is effective in supporting food-insecure communities and promoting sustainable development, and that the organization is well-positioned to continue its efforts in this area. However, the growing impact of climate change on humanitarian needs requires WFP to redouble its fundraising efforts to ensure that its programs and operations are climate-compatible and risk-informed.

This evaluation aims to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) resilience strengthening efforts in achieving its overarching vision of enabling people to better manage shocks and stressors while improving their food security and nutrition. To achieve this objective, the evaluation will examine the implementation of WFP's resilience policy, which focuses on empowering women, girls, and marginalized people, improving livelihoods, and enhancing natural, physical, financial, human, and social capital. The evaluation will also assess the organization's capacity to leverage its convening role, expand strategic and operational partnerships, and invest in data, research, and evidence generation to support accountability, funding decisions, and programme design.

The evaluation will employ a mixed-methods approach, combining both quantitative and qualitative data to assess the impact and effectiveness of WFP's resilience programmes. Key findings will include the identification of best practices, lessons learned, and areas for improvement in WFP's resilience programming. The evaluation will also examine the organization's capacity to adapt to changing contexts, including the impact of conflict and climate change on resilience programming.

The implications of this evaluation will inform WFP's future resilience programming, including the development of new policies, strategies, and guidelines. The evaluation will also provide recommendations for strengthening partnerships, investing in capacity building, and leveraging data and research to support evidence-based decision-making. Ultimately, the evaluation aims to contribute to the global knowledge and practices in the area of resilience, with a focus on improving food security and nutrition outcomes for vulnerable populations.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) school meal programmes in promoting sustainable development and humanitarian outcomes. The evaluation objective was to inform WFP's strategic plan and policy framework for school meal programming. The methodology involved reviewing existing evidence, policies, and programme documents, as well as engaging with stakeholders and partners. Key findings highlighted the critical role of school meal programmes in promoting health, nutrition, education, and social protection outcomes, particularly for vulnerable children and families. The evaluation also identified opportunities for WFP to enhance its support for governments in designing and implementing nationally owned school meal programmes that meet national development goals. Implications of the evaluation include the need for WFP to continue its shift from being an implementer of programmes to becoming an enabler of country efforts, with a focus on promoting local ownership and sustainability, and supporting the growth of the School Meals Coalition to mobilize political will and increase domestic resource allocations for school meals.

This evaluation aims to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) school feeding initiatives in promoting sustainable and equitable food systems, particularly in fragile and low-income countries. The evaluation methodology involved a review of existing literature and case studies of WFP's interventions in 30 countries, including the implementation of the Transformative Schools Feeding Model and the Energising Home Grown School Feeding project. Key findings indicate that WFP's school feeding programmes can effectively address challenges such as malnutrition, environmental degradation, and climate change by promoting healthy and sustainable food habits, supporting local agriculture, and creating demand for planet-friendly food production practices. The evaluation also highlights the potential of schools as laboratories for demonstrating the benefits of clean cooking and low-carbon energy solutions, as well as the importance of leveraging food procurement for school meals to influence food systems. Implications of these findings suggest that national governments and international agencies can play a crucial role in promoting sustainable and equitable food systems by integrating sustainability considerations into context-specific and evidence-informed standards for school meals, supporting local smallholder farmers, and investing in clean and energy-efficient cooking solutions.

This evaluation synthesis aims to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) engagement in middle-income countries (MICs) between 2019 and 2024. To achieve this objective, the synthesis analyzed 73 centralized and decentralized evaluations conducted in 25 MICs, focusing on WFP's partnerships, resource mobilization, and strategic shifts in its work. The key findings indicate that WFP's programmes in MICs are resourced at similar levels as those in low-income countries, with around 57 percent of their needs-based plans funded in 2024. The evaluations also show that WFP's role in MICs has evolved over time, reflecting changing national circumstances and operational needs. However, the synthesis notes that WFP's approach to partnerships in MICs lacks a coherent and overarching framework, and that the organization's engagement in MICs is often constrained by external perceptions of WFP as a specialist humanitarian-response agency. Furthermore, the synthesis highlights the importance of WFP's convening partnerships and brokering knowledge in MICs, as well as its potential role in supporting governments to identify and prioritize national food security and nutrition needs. The implications of these findings suggest that WFP needs to develop a more comprehensive partnership framework for MICs and strengthen its capacity to engage in policy advocacy and systems strengthening work in these countries.

This evaluation aimed to assess the World Food Programme's (WFP) role in addressing youth employment, a critical issue affecting food security and overall development. The study employed a global literature review of youth employment programmes and WFP programming, as well as case studies in various countries. Key findings indicate that the youth unemployment crisis is compounded by high levels of informal employment, characterized by poor working conditions, low pay, and limited access to social protection services. The study highlights the need for WFP to think strategically about how it can contribute to youth employment outcomes, particularly in countries where a large proportion of the population is young and food-insecure. The evaluation suggests that WFP can leverage its comparative advantage to bring the voices of young, food-insecure people into debates about youth employment and contribute to responses that deliver long-term, sustainable change. To achieve this, WFP should develop a more deliberate and focused approach to addressing youth employment, including mainstreaming support for youth employment within its work, recognizing the intersectional barriers young women and men face, and outlining an organisational strategy for addressing youth employment.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) interventions in the Pacific Island Countries and Territories (PICTs) in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by 2030. The evaluation methodology involved an analysis of WFP's Multi-Country Strategic Plan (MCSP) 2023-2027, which is aligned with the 2050 Strategy for the Blue Pacific Continent and the United Nations Pacific Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework. Key findings indicate that PICTs face significant challenges in achieving the SDGs due to growing inequality, gender inequity, and insufficient public services. To address these challenges, WFP has implemented various initiatives, including the Anticipatory Action pilot project in Fiji, macro insurance through the Pacific Catastrophe Risk Insurance Company, and capacity building through a micro-accreditation programme for humanitarian supply chain and logistics. These initiatives aim to enhance the resilience of PICTs to climate and disaster shocks, improve access to national social protection systems, and foster the ability of people to meet their food security, nutrition, and associated essential needs. The evaluation highlights WFP's efforts to support PICTs in achieving the SDGs, including the provision of humanitarian air services and technical assistance during the COVID-19 pandemic and a severe drought in Kiribati.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the R4 Rural Resilience Initiative in enhancing food security and building resilience of beneficiary households and their communities in Zimbabwe. The evaluation employed a decentralized activity evaluation methodology, involving a consortium of Particip and Jimat, and utilized a range of data collection methods, including focus group discussions, phone surveys, and interviews with beneficiaries, WFP staff, and national IP staff. The evaluation sought to answer the overarching question: "To what extent is the R4 initiative as part of the integrated risk management interventions effective in enhancing food security and building resilience of beneficiary households and their communities?" Key findings include: the R4 Initiative has improved or stabilized food security status and increased livelihood security and resilience among targeted populations; the initiative has also improved investment capacity, natural resource management, and climate shock resilience. However, challenges in mobilizing field-level Government support and adapting to the financial uncertainties of the Covid-19 pandemic have affected the program's implementation. The evaluation suggests that subsequent actions should aim for a minimum of five years engagement with farmers to achieve sustainable results. Implications of the evaluation include the need to explore options for linking R4 to national social protection systems, ensuring community resources for maintaining R4, and identifying medium-term risks to reduce sustainability risks.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of the UNAIDS Joint Programme in promoting sustainable and efficient financing for the AIDS response, with a focus on its role in supporting countries to achieve the 2030 goal of ending AIDS as a public health threat. The evaluation employed a mixed-methods approach, combining stakeholder interviews, country case studies, and analysis of global strategies and reports. Key findings indicate that the Joint Programme has played a crucial role in increasing political commitment for HIV, but has struggled to translate this into material change in domestic financing. The evaluation also highlights the need for the Joint Programme to better align its work on efficiency and sustainability of AIDS funding with the new Global AIDS Strategy 2021-2026, which recognizes the importance of Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in the HIV response. Furthermore, the evaluation suggests that the Joint Programme requires more resources to engage at the provincial level, where HIV financing decisions are now being made. The evaluation concludes that the Joint Programme has contributed to resource efficiencies in the HIV response, but areas for improvement remain, including further consideration of allocative and technical efficiencies and better linkage of strategic information work to changes in funding flows. Overall, the evaluation recommends that the Joint Programme prioritize building its capacity in UHC and UHC financing, and strengthen its partnerships with governments, civil society, and international partners to improve sustainable financing and efficiency for AIDS.

This evaluation aimed to assess the effectiveness of various humanitarian interventions. The evaluation methodology involved a comprehensive review of existing literature, accessed on May 1, 2023. Key findings indicate that the interventions had a positive impact on the target population, with notable improvements in access to essential services and overall well-being. However, the evaluation also highlighted challenges and limitations, including resource constraints and contextual factors that affected the interventions' effectiveness. The implications of these findings suggest that humanitarian organizations should prioritize context-specific programming, invest in capacity building, and ensure adequate resource allocation to maximize the impact of their interventions.
